metadata.title: Legend of the Rood: Linguistic Glossary
metadata.description: Specialized Middle Cornish vocabulary found in the Ordinalia and the Legend of the Rood cycle.

terms.definition: A central theme of the Fall. It describes the physical and spiritual distress Adam feels after exile.
Divine favor. Often used to describe the properties of the 'Oil of Mercy' or the holiness of the Rood tree.
terms.etymology: Borrowed from Middle English 'grace', ultimately Latin 'gratia'.

terms.definition: The promised spiritual healing requested by Adam at his death. In the Rood legend, this 'oil' is fulfilled by Christ's blood on the Cross.
The physical structure made from the Cedar, Cypress, and Pine grown from Adam's seeds.
The emotional state associated with Paradise and the Resurrection. The linguistic opposite of 'Anken'.
Often used to refer to the 'Holy Wood' throughout its various stages (rod, beam, cross).
Used in titles like 'Map Den' (Son of Man).
Commonly found in titles of Cornish miracle plays (e.g., Bewnans Ke).
Specifically used in reference to the 'Forbidden Fruit' in Act I.
